section.title: Pull and push to a remote repository
section.p: Pulling and pushing is one of the most common workflows in git. If you are unfamiliar with it, go to the git website.
Push commits to add changes to a repository's current branch. The repository can be local or remote.
Use push to commit changes to the current branch and create a record of those changes with a commit message.
If your local branch is associated with a remote branch, pull changes or verify that the branches have not diverged before pushing your changes to avoid file conflicts.
To push changes, follow these steps:

section.title: Pulling commits
section.p: Pull commits to bring your local branch up to date with its associated remote branch.
